_metadata.purpose: Machine-readable provenance catalog for NCRB 2024 calibration data used in NEXUS synthetic data generation

provenance_model.NCRB_DERIVED: Directly read from a specific NCRB table cell with exact row/column
provenance_model.NCRB_INFERRED: Computed from NCRB cells via an explicit, documented formula
provenance_model.SYNTHETIC_ASSUMPTION: Design choice not supported by available NCRB files

source_files.description: Districtwise SLL Crimes - 2024 (All India, all districts)
source_files.important_note: SLL crimes are a SEPARATE register from IPC/BNS. Do NOT sum with IPC totals without explicit mixed-register documentation.

key_column.col59: Total Cyber Crimes (A. IT Act + B. IPC Cyber + C. SLL Cyber)

source_files.important_note: Cyber crimes cross-cut both IPC and SLL registers. The col59 total is a combined count and must NOT be added to IPC or SLL totals separately.

calibration_parameters.recommendation: Obtain NCRB Table 10A for defensible source.

calibration_parameters.reason: NCRB Table 10A not in current files. 10DistrictwiseMissingPersons2024 provides MISSING PERSON age data which cannot serve as accused age proxy.
calibration_parameters.recommendation: Obtain NCRB Table 10A for defensible source.

calibration_parameters.reason: NCRB Table 5A (Victims of IPC Crimes) not in current files. TABLE3B13 covers metropolitan cities crime-against-women rate, not general victim gender.
TABLE1B44 headers contain section references but provide crime counts by city, not a canonical section mapping. Manually curated and labeled as such.
calibration_parameters.table1b44_finding: Row4 column headers embed BNS/IPC section numbers within crime-head labels (e.g., 'Rape (Section 64 to Section 71 BNS)') — informative but not authoritative.

calibration_parameters.reason: NCRB aggregate tables contain no personal name distribution. Name pools are synthetic realism inputs reflecting Karnataka's multilingual demographics.

NCRB aggregate crime counts cannot establish that criminal networks traverse specific geographic axes. The Bengaluru-Mangaluru and Bengaluru-Hubballi axes are synthetic scenario topology, not NCRB-derived relationships.

assumptions: Accused gender (88% male) is a design prior, NOT NCRB-derived
Accused age distribution (peak 18-35) is a design prior, NOT NCRB-derived
Victim gender (55% male) is a design prior, NOT NCRB-derived
BNS section mapping is manually curated, informed by TABLE1B44 headers but NOT sourced from them
Name pools are synthetic realism inputs, NOT NCRB-derived
Criminal network topology (degree, clustering, community size) is NOT NCRB-derived
Cross-jurisdiction network axes are synthetic scenario assumptions, NOT NCRB-derived
NEXUS_CASE_STATUS_WEIGHTS use all-India proxy for Karnataka (Karnataka-specific unavailable)
SLL crime weights are NOT mixed into IPC probability vectors to prevent double-counting
limitations: NCRB Table 10A (Persons Arrested by Age and Sex) not available — accused age/gender remain assumptions
NCRB Table 5A (Victims of IPC Crimes) not available — victim gender remains assumption
Karnataka-specific case disposal data not available — all-India proxy used for status weights
District-level crime data is for 2024 only — multi-year trend calibration not possible with current files
Cyber crime data cross-cuts IPC and SLL registers — combined Bengaluru cyber figure includes both
9 of 19 NCRB files are unused in current calibration (TABLE1C44, TABLE2B14, TABLE2B24, TABLE2D16, TABLE2D29, TABLE3B23, TABLE4B13, TABLE4B23, TABLE8B13, TABLE9B23) — available for future enhancement
